relevance.rationale: The corpus opened a live derivation route on 2026-08-07 (docs/audits/2026-08-07-extended-bloch-group-fixes-the-normalization-fit.md, beans qou-78pt / qou-l2t2) whose central claim is verbatim 'Neumann's extended Bloch group is the canonical resolution of exactly that ambiguity' — the branch-of-logarithm ambiguity that made the Markov-normalization route a fit. Corpus-grep for that route's source: references.ts registers neumann-zagier1985 (the 1985 volumes paper) and nothing else by Neumann; there is NO registered source for the extended Bloch group at all, and grep for 'extended Bloch' finds only that audit, a companion audit, one coordination doc, and QOU/QBeta/BlochFiveTerm.lean. So a route the corpus is actively building on has zero bibliography backing. This document's §3 is exactly that missing statement: I read pp.7-9 and it gives the Bloch group B(F) as ker(d: Z[F] -> Lambda^2 F^x) modulo the 5-term relation, the extended Bloch group with the lifted 5-term relation on pairs (u,v) with e^u = 1 - e^v, and the extended regulator into C/4pi^2 Z whose imaginary and real parts are volume and Chern-Simons. §4 additionally gives the half-symplectic completion of the Neumann-Zagier matrix H = (A B), which is the structure behind the det J_NZ(B_3) object the corpus's 1-loop witness uses. Honest scope caveat: this is a SURVEY, so it is an authoritative statement plus a pointer, not the original theorem; the primary sources for the extended Bloch group are cited inside it as its [30] (Neumann) and [21,39] (Zickert, Goette) and those should be registered too if the route matures. I am rating it core because the corpus demonstrably should be citing an extended-Bloch-group source right now and cites none.

keyResults.statement: The extended Bloch group is generated by pairs (u,v) with e^u = 1 - e^v modulo a lifted 5-term relation, and carries an extended regulator to C/4pi^2 Z given by L(u,v) = Li_2-type term + uv/2 - pi^2/6, whose value is the complexified volume Vol + i CS.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the published statement that the branch/framing ambiguity of a complex multiplicative invariant has a canonical lift — the assertion docs/audits/2026-08-07-extended-bloch-group-fixes-the-normalization-fit.md makes with no source. It also gives the additive-over-ideal-tetrahedra form the audit's extensivity argument relies on.

keyResults.statement: The Neumann-Zagier matrix H = (A B) formed from edge and peripheral equations is half-symplectic over Z, and this follows from the Neumann chain complex 0 -> C_0 -> C_1 -> J -> C_1 -> C_0 -> 0.
keyResults.useForFolio: The corpus consumes det J_NZ(B_3) in its 1-loop / Borromean witness but has only neumann-zagier1985 registered; the integral (not merely rational) symplectic refinement stated here is the property that determinant computation actually needs.

proposedActions.rationale: The 2026-08-07 extended-Bloch-group route has no registered source for its central object; this survey is the citable statement of it.

def:quantum-bloch-group and conj:borromean-bloch-group-element both state Bloch-group/regulator facts (5-term relation, Beilinson regulator = Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm, volume as regulator evaluation) without a source for the extended/lifted version now being used downstream.

The corpus should record explicitly that the extended Bloch group, not the ordinary one, is what resolves the branch ambiguity — and that the primary sources cited inside this survey (Neumann; Zickert; Goette) still need registering before any Lean statement leans on the lifted 5-term relation.

relevance.rationale: A survey of Walter Neumann's work on triangulation combinatorics and its K-theoretic interactions: gluing equations, volumes and Dehn surgeries, the Bloch group and the extended Bloch group, the symplectic properties of NZ data, quantisation of the NZ Lagrangian, and number-theoretic connections. Three separate corpus items sit on this material: conj:borromean-bloch-group-element (a K_3(C)/Bloch-group class with regulator 8G), prop:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin (Bloch group, Suslin's isomorphism, archimedean evaluation of Li_2^q), and def:quantum-bloch-group. Supporting rather than core: it is a survey, and the theorems it recounts are Neumann-Zagier 1985 and Neumann's own papers, both of which the corpus can and partly does cite directly. Its distinctive value is that it puts the extended Bloch group (home of the complex volume) and the quantisation of the NZ Lagrangian (the kinematical kernel of the state integral) in one place, which is precisely the bridge between the corpus's two currently-disjoint faces. IMPORTANT: this is NOT the existing ref garoufalidis-zagier2023, which is arXiv:2304.09377 'Knots and their related q-series' -- the two arXiv ids are adjacent and easy to confuse.

keyResults.locator: Sect. 3 (The Bloch group and the extended Bloch group)
keyResults.statement: Construction of the extended Bloch group and the chain complex in which it sits, as the home of the complex-volume invariant.
keyResults.useForFolio: The natural citation for the corpus's 8G regulator claim and for the group in which the corpus's fraktur-V = Vol + i CS analogy actually lives; conj:borromean-bloch-group-element currently asserts a K_3(C) class without pointing at the extended-Bloch construction.

keyResults.statement: Quantisation of the shape and Ptolemy variables of an ideal triangulation, in which the kinematical kernel is the quantisation of the Neumann-Zagier Lagrangian, described also via cluster X- and A-coordinates.
keyResults.useForFolio: Connects the corpus's NZ/1-loop side (computations/one_loop_torsion.py, det J_NZ) to its state-integral / Phi_b side in a single statement; the folio currently treats these as separate programmes.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry, and the closest existing key (garoufalidis-zagier2023) is a different paper with an adjacent arXiv id; minting a distinct id and noting the near-collision in its note field prevents a mis-keyed citation later.
conj:borromean-bloch-group-element asserts a nontrivial Bloch-group / K_3(C) class with regulator 8G; the extended-Bloch-group construction it relies on has no citation in the block.
